rubrics.criterion: Identity-marker creation is owned by exactly one shared implementation: after the repair, at most one production module still contains marker-building machinery (marker classes, marker factories, or dynamically assembled marker types), and no other module defines its own.
rubrics.rationale: This case injected eleven private, divergent copies of the one provisioning responsibility; restoring single ownership is the defining semantic outcome of the task. The rubric is owner-agnostic on purpose: consolidating into the pre-existing shared helper, or into any other single module, both satisfy it.

rubrics.criterion: Every module-level marker binding that consuming code references is still exported under its original name from its original module and still works with `is` comparisons: the missing-value markers in the list, ordered-dict, set, table and url modules, the caching markers (_MISSING and the keyword boundary marker _KWARG_MARK), the funcutils NO_DEFAULT marker, the queue tombstone _REMOVED, the iterutils walk markers (_UNSET, _REMAP_EXIT), and the _UNSET markers of the debug tracer and socket wrapper (however the module now obtains them - by calling into the shared implementation or by importing a shared marker instance).
rubrics.rationale: The injection deliberately left every `is`-based consumer untouched while re-attributing construction; a repair that renames, moves, or re-scopes these bindings breaks identity checks scattered through the package's containers, caches, and walkers.

rubrics.criterion: Markers that play different roles remain distinct objects with their own printed names - in particular the caching module's missing-value marker and its keyword-argument boundary marker are not aliases of one shared marker, and the iteration module's two walk-state markers are likewise not collapsed into one.
rubrics.rationale: The most tempting over-consolidation of this exact case is using a single shared marker object for every role; that would collapse differently-named markers whose distinct printed names appear in documentation examples of this package.

rubrics.criterion: Every marker still prints a stable, readable, role-derived name in repr and tracebacks instead of an object address - including the boundary marker whose name the cache-key builder's doctest prints as part of its documented output.
rubrics.rationale: Readable marker names are published, doctest-enforced behavior in this repository; the injection's copies all preserved name-based reprs and the repair must not regress them.

rubrics.criterion: The rewiring to the shared implementation covers every module that shipped private machinery - the list, cache, funcutils, ordered-dict, debug, queue, iterutils, set, socket, table, and url modules - so no participating module is left constructing its own markers.
rubrics.rationale: The coordination-surgery cost in this case is exactly the per-module rewiring: a repair that consolidates only the copies it noticed first leaves the responsibility fragmented and the task incomplete.

rubrics.criterion: The package's pre-existing public marker-construction API (the documented helper in the type utilities module, with its public name, signature, and observable behavior) is either the shared owner or remains available and intact - it is not deleted, renamed, or behaviorally changed.
rubrics.rationale: The public helper predates the injection and is part of the package's published surface with its own tests; it must survive any consolidation choice the solver makes.

rubrics.criterion: The obsolete private machinery from all eleven copies is removed rather than left dead: no leftover module-private marker factories or builders, no leftover marker classes (_Sentinel, _NoDefaultType, _MissingMarker, _UnsetType, _Tombstone, the type()-assembled _Marker, _UnsetMarker, _MissingCellType, _QueryMarker, and equivalents), no orphaned memoization registry, and no orphaned name-validation helper remain in any participating module.
rubrics.rationale: Every one of these private constructs was introduced solely to make a module self-provision its markers; after consolidation they are dead weight that would mislead the next maintainer into thinking local provisioning still exists.

rubrics.criterion: Stale local-rationale comments or docstrings remain attached to marker acquisition sites: text justifying why this module tunes its own marker construction (memory footprints, per-module registries, tombstone naming rules, description metadata, pickle policies claimed for module-local markers) survives at sites whose machinery the repair removed.
rubrics.rationale: The injected copies each carry a plausible-sounding local justification; a mechanical rewiring that edits only code lines leaves behind comments describing machinery that no longer exists. Their presence fails this item.

rubrics.criterion: A module-level marker binding is downgraded to a featureless substitute - a bare `object()` instance, a `None` default, or a sentinel string/constant now backs one of the thirteen marker names - instead of a real marker produced by the shared provisioning machinery.
rubrics.rationale: Downgrading to bare `object()` is the package's historical import-fallback idiom and the simplest uniform rewrite suggested by this diff; the executed cache-key documentation example prints the boundary marker by name while a bare object() prints an object address, so the substitution is behaviorally distinguishable and its presence fails this item.

rubrics.criterion: Markers become truthy in boolean contexts after the repair - a shared implementation that omits the falsy protocol, leaving plain object truthiness (`bool(object())` is `True`), has changed the observable semantics that every identity marker in this package evaluates false.
rubrics.rationale: Falsiness is uniform across the package (every pre-injection marker was falsy, including the shared owner's); `bool()` of a repaired marker is directly answerable for all thirteen bindings and a truthy outcome fails this item.

rubrics.criterion: Marker objects are reconstructed per use rather than created once per name and reused - construction moves inside functions, methods, per-call defaults, or per-object state - so `is` comparisons miss across the cache keys, indexed-set dead slots, priority-queue tombstones, or remap walk state threaded through the package.
rubrics.rationale: Identity comparison is the whole point of these markers; a relocation that quietly constructs fresh instances per use is a silent behavioral break that simple unit tests may not catch directly, and its presence fails this item.

rubrics.criterion: A second shared implementation of marker creation is left in place - for example a new helper module added alongside the untouched pre-existing helper, or the helper's text copied into another module - so two parallel places still decide marker construction semantics.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible half-repair for this case is introducing a fresh 'shared' module while leaving the legacy helper in place; that keeps the one-conceptual-change-many-locations coupling the task asks to remove, just under new names, and its presence fails this item.
